review.summary: Phase 21 delivers substantial, genuinely verifiable planning and provenance work, and its recorded evidence is real rather than asserted. I independently confirmed: the vendored management 0.86.0 corpus is byte-pinned in three places (contracts/manifest.json:1950-1963 source + :2442-2483 four vendorArtifacts, contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/source.json:13-15) with an MIT license entry, and tools/verify-contracts.py:29,393-407,471-489 owns exactly that subtree without absorbing the data-plane or Portkey trees, with 27 self-test tampering rejections including ten new vendor-ownership cases. The seven-source/160-operation inventory reproduces with full per-operation parameters, body, responses, security, servers and recursive reference closure (contracts/airs-operations.json, 160 coverage rows; contracts/vendor/.../operations.json, 42 operationIds), each bound to a type-qualified native Rust method that the tool proves exists. All 68 management deltas carry a category and decision with lossless old/new values, affectedOperations and successorReferences, and tools/red_team_management.py:148-198 genuinely fails closed on removals, requiredness, security, non-schema and parameter-set changes, with 17 digest-pinned semantic changes. The retention floor is independent and immutable: contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json and contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json both carry 4279 baselineIds, matching contracts/native-exports.json (3820) plus contracts/native-operations.json (448) plus 11 extras exactly, and --verify-retention-origin rehashes all six ledgers. Every design claim in the plan that I checked against actual bytes held: TargetConnectionType gains only VERTEX_AI and N8N, ResponseMode gains REALTIME, ProfilingStatusFilter is exactly the four claimed values, TargetStatusFilter narrows from seven frozen values to DRAFT/ACTIVE (so the whole migration table is grounded), the frozen ProfilingStatus did contain INIT and QUEUED, the four Vertex fields and three regex patterns exist with a real four-entry allowlist at crates/scm-sdk/src/validation.rs:1058-1063 to extend, MultiTurnClientSessionConfig carries a vendor default the plan deliberately refuses to insert, BasicAuth fields were previously tolerated unknown keys, and the five target response declarations match. Governance is equally concrete: the >=9/10 plan gate exists and is tested (tools/review_phase.py:70), the fifth-attempt exception requires four substantive priors, later phases fail closed, the CI subset cannot qualify a review, and the 23 recorded checks match tools/check_phase.py:135-170 element for element with every exit code 0 at the reviewed hash e2a407ab, plus a private-material scan re-bound to that same fingerprint. What keeps this below the phase bar is that none of the findings from the two accepted attempt-03 chunk reviews were addressed - the source hash is unchanged, so all five plan-and-provenance and five governance findings persist - and I found two more. Three mediums stand: disposition() fails open on constraint leaves outside its reviewed-digest set (added enum/pattern, changed default/additionalProperties/bounds), which is the classifier phase 25 inherits; contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json is a 27,250-line duplicate of the immutable seed plus three keys, discarding every value computed at lines 382-393 so --check can never see ledger additions and the count tests assert the floor copy; and docs/CI.md:182-195 claims in present tense that the phase gate invokes scripts/check-dependencies.py and prepares the locked graph for it, when commands_for(21) contains no dependency audit at all, while .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:62-69 still builds cargo-audit and cargo-deny from source for no consumer and tools/test_ci.py:167-170 actively requires those dead steps. Additionally the phase-20 accepted-with-deficiencies outcome required the docs/RELEASE.md authorization paragraph to be scheduled explicitly rather than deferred again; phase 21 edits that file as declared scope but line 160 still names only 0.1.1 and 0.2.0, with no carry-forward record anywhere in phase-status. No blocker or high finding; dependency exposure is mitigated because Cargo.lock is byte-frozen against the audited commit. Categories 9/8/8/9/9 = 43/50, below the 46/50 phase floor, and 8.5/10 is below the >=9 plan gate.

findings.description: disposition() documents itself as failing "closed on unclassified changes" (line 149), but the REVIEWED_SEMANTIC_CHANGES digest requirement applies only when kind == 'changed' AND path[-1] is one of {type, format, enum, anyOf, oneOf, $ref}. Two classes of semantic change therefore reach the schema-name classifier at lines 182-197 and receive an automatic category with no reviewed digest: (a) any kind == 'added' constraint leaf, e.g. an 'enum' or 'pattern' added to an existing property of TargetSchema, which falls through to line 196 and returns 'new_behavior_and_alias'; (b) kind == 'changed' for constraint keys absent from the set, notably additionalProperties, default, const, pattern, items, maxLength, minLength, maximum and minimum. A vendor flip of additionalProperties true->false, or a changed default on an existing property, would be silently recorded as reviewed new behavior. I verified this is currently unexercised: of the 68 deltas in compatibility-decisions.json there are 29 'changed' rows, and they decompose exactly into the 17 digest-pinned paths, 11 annotation-only 'documentation' rows and the one ['paths','/v1/target','get','parameters'] row, so no unpinned constraint change exists today. The gap matters because this is the classifier the phase 25 drift detection and the next upstream re-pin inherit, and the plan at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:235-237 promises "Unknown changes fail classification". Defaults and open-object acceptance are behavior-critical in this codebase (G10/G25).
findings.required_fix: Apply the reviewed-digest requirement to any delta whose leaf key is a schema constraint keyword regardless of kind, and extend the keyword set to at least additionalProperties, default, const, pattern, maxLength, minLength, maximum, minimum, maxItems, minItems and items. Add regressions in tools/test_red_team_management.py asserting 'Unclassified' for an added 'enum' on an existing property and for a changed 'default' and 'additionalProperties' leaf.

findings.description: retained_floor() returns {**floor, 'seed', 'seedSha256', 'preservationCheck'}, so the emitted contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json is the immutable seed plus exactly three keys. I confirmed this by comparing top-level keys of both files: they are identical apart from preservationCheck/seed/seedSha256 (airs-retained-capabilities.json:27158,27249-27250 vs contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json), and both contain 4279 baselineIds across ~27,250 lines. Three consequences. First, the repository tracks two near-identical 27k-line artifacts. Second, every value computed at lines 382-393 - 'policy', 'preservedPolicies', 'evidenceLimit', 'baselineCommit', 'schemaVersion' and the freshly extracted exports/methods/defaultBindings/extra queries - is discarded for output and exists only as the comparison operand, which is not evident from the code and has no comment saying so. Third, because the output is a floor copy, the --check byte comparison of this artifact can never detect additions to the current ledgers, and tools/test_red_team_management.py:58-66 asserts 3820/448/23/14/11/2 against the floor copy rather than the freshly extracted ledgers. The plan at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:43-44 describes the artifact as an inventory of "3820 frozen export mappings, 448 native methods, 23 default bindings", which reads as current state; the numbers happen to coincide today because current equals floor, so this is misleading rather than wrong.
findings.required_fix: Either stop emitting the duplicate - keep contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json as the single floor and have the tool emit a small provenance/verification receipt - or emit the actual current inventory and record the floor by reference with its seed hash. Rename the local at line 382 to make clear it is a comparison operand, and reassert the 3820/448/23/14 counts against the freshly extracted ledgers in tools/test_red_team_management.py.

findings.description: The "Dependency and target evidence" section states in the present tense that "The phase gate invokes scripts/check-dependencies.py; it refreshes and records official RustSec provenance, audits the complete Cargo lock with warnings denied, and checks all-feature license/source/ban policy" (182-186), and that "The qualification job fetches the complete locked dependency graph without a target filter, then resolves all-feature metadata offline before the phase gate. The current dependency audit inventories all targets" (192-195). Neither is true of the gate this phase routes CI to. commands_for(21) (tools/check_phase.py:147-170) contains no dependency audit, and ci_commands_for only removes commands (check_phase.py:644-646); the only scripts/ entry in the 23 executed commands is scripts/check-private-material.py, as the recorded run confirms (docs/reviews/phase-21-attempt-01.checks.json:293-304). Consequently .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:62-69 - "Install exact dependency-policy tools" building cargo-audit 0.22.2 and cargo-deny 0.20.2 from source, then "Prepare locked dependency inputs for the policy audit" with cargo fetch --locked and cargo metadata - has no consumer in the contracts job: the gate needs only rustfmt for tools/generate_models.py:1070, and the cargo invocation at generate_models.py:1026-1027 belongs to --verify-fixtures, which is not in the list. Every remote run therefore spends several minutes on unused source builds. The lockstep tests sanction rather than catch this: tools/test_ci.py:60-65 compares the documented inventory only against the "## Scripts run by the current contracts gate" section (which correctly lists one script), :67-68 and :172-175 add explicit phase-21 exemptions, and :167-170 positively asserts the dead fetch/metadata steps exist before the gate. Dependency exposure itself is mitigated, because Cargo.lock is byte-frozen against 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e by commands_for(21)[0] and advisory coverage returns at phases 22-25 via the inherited phase-20 list, but the boundary is undocumented and a declared-scope artifact carries a false current-state claim.
findings.required_fix: Make documentation, workflow and tests agree. Either add ["python", "scripts/check-dependencies.py", "--output", "docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json"] to management_commands(21), list it in the docs/CI.md:150-152 inventory and drop the test_ci.py:67-68 exemption; or remove the unused .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:62-69 steps, rewrite docs/CI.md:181-195 into explicitly historical phase-8/17/20 tense with a sentence stating that the Phase 21 planning gate runs no dependency or advisory audit and that it resumes at phase 22, and replace the test_ci.py:172-175 phase-21 branch with an assertion that locked-graph preparation exists only when a selected command consumes it. Re-run tools/check_phase.py --phase 21 so the bound snapshot matches the new list.

findings.description: The publication authorization paragraph still reads "Maintainer authorization covers 0.1.1 and the subsequent 0.2.0 delivery recorded in the release plan", although 0.2.1 and 0.2.2 have since been published. This was raised three times in phase 20 and carried into its accepted_with_deficiencies outcome, where the required fix states explicitly that it "cannot be done inside phase 20 without breaking the registry readiness and CI source binding, so it must be scheduled explicitly rather than left as an open deferral" (docs/phase-status.json:4958-4959). Phase 21 declares docs/RELEASE.md in its phase-governance chunk scope (docs/phase-status.json:5058) and does modify the file (line 9 now documents the --phase 21 routing), so this was the qualified source change in which the fix or an explicit schedule was due. Neither happened: the paragraph is unchanged, and grepping docs/phase-status.json for scheduling language finds only the phase-20 text itself, with no carry-forward entry in phase 21's review_findings_disposition. A maintainer consulting the release procedure before the 0.2.3 delivery still reads an inaccurate authorization statement.
findings.required_fix: Extend the paragraph to name the 0.2.1 (portkey-access-policies-plan.md) and 0.2.2 (g25-response-compatibility-plan.md) deliveries and their authorizing plans, or, if the edit must wait for phase 24, add an explicit carry-forward entry to phase 21's review_findings_disposition in docs/phase-status.json naming this finding, its owning phase and the milestone that closes it, so it is scheduled rather than silently deferred a fourth time.

findings.description: review_findings_disposition.reviews lists only the four attempt-01 and attempt-02 chunk records and omits both docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-plan-and-provenance-attempt-03.json and docs/reviews/phase-21-chunk-phase-governance-attempt-03.json, even though the sibling decisions map (5104-5173) includes them and the note at 5081 explicitly reasons about "Current attempt03 chunks pass (governance44, provenance43)". The attempt-03 records are the only ones bound to the current source hash e2a407ab and the only ones that can authorize advancement under accepted_chunks (tools/review_phase.py:289-346), so the authoritative list in the status file is both incomplete and inconsistent with the block that depends on it. This is the partially-applied remainder of governance attempt-03 finding 3, which asked for per-attempt decisions and totals; the decisions map was added but the reviews array was not refreshed.
findings.required_fix: Append both attempt-03 record paths to review_findings_disposition.reviews, or replace the array with the decisions map as the single list so the two cannot diverge, and add a regression in tools/test_management_phases.py asserting that every key of decisions appears in reviews for the active phase.

findings.description: The management corpus ships a source.json recording expectedOperations 42, openapiVersion 3.1.0, apiVersion 0.86.0, sha256/bytes/gitBlobSha1, licensePath/licenseSha256/licenseSpdx and the js-yaml 4.3.2 pin, but no tool reads any of it. tools/red_team_management.py derives everything from contracts/manifest.json plus the hash-pinned audit inventory and never asserts spec['openapi'] == '3.1.0' or cross-checks the license digest, while tools/verify-contracts.py only tracks the file's bytes and compares repository/commit/license against the manifest source entry, not the file's internal fields. The equivalent data-plane corpus is treated as an authority by tools/red_team_dataplane.py, which validates its expectedOperations and openapiVersion. The recorded values are consistent with the manifest today, so this is latent, but the inconsistent pattern invites a reader to trust an unverified file.
findings.required_fix: In red_team_management.build(), load VENDOR/'source.json' and assert its path, sha256, bytes, licensePath/licenseSha256, openapiVersion, apiVersion and expectedOperations against the actual YAML bytes, the license file, spec['openapi'], spec['info']['version'] and the operation count, mirroring the data-plane loader, with a test that each mismatch raises.

findings.description: impl_contains() strips raw strings (203), normal strings (204) and char literals (205) before stripping comments (206). A line comment containing an unpaired double quote, for example // don"t, is therefore tokenized as the start of a string literal, and the DOTALL string regex blanks everything up to the next quote anywhere later in the file. That can hide a genuinely present inherent method, producing a false "Missing Rust function", or, by removing a closing brace, make the prefix.count('{') == prefix.count('}') test at line 217 succeed for a nested fn and admit a binding that is not an inherent method. The only existing regression (tools/test_red_team_management.py:111) covers a string containing a brace. Static native-binding verification is the weakest link in the "all 160 operations are mapped to native methods" claim, so its tokenizer ordering matters even though no current SDK source triggers it.
findings.required_fix: Strip line and block comments before strings, or tokenize comments and string literals in a single pass, and add a regression in tools/test_red_team_management.py using a source whose line comment contains an unbalanced double quote while its impl genuinely defines the method.

findings.description: REVIEWED_SEMANTIC_CHANGES binds 17 reviewed semantic changes to sha256(encoded(identity)) digests over the path/kind/old/new subset, which is a good tamper binding, but there is no documented or tooled way to produce those digests at the next upstream re-pin. The failure message at line 155, "Unclassified semantic value change: {path}", tells a maintainer nothing about the artifact required, and neither the module docstring nor the source-authority section of docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md describes the procedure. Phase 25 explicitly re-pins a complete new pan.dev tree, so this path will be hit by design.
findings.required_fix: Document the digest-construction procedure (identity = the path/kind/old/new subset, canonicalised by encoded()) in the module docstring and in the plan's source-authority section, and have the error path print the old/new values with an instruction to review them and register the computed digest, so the step is reproducible without reading the implementation.

findings.description: The data-plane row records activeSourceId "vendor:red-team-dp:0.93.0", hardcoded at tools/red_team_management.py:332. That identifier resolves to nothing: contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/source.json has no "id" field, and the 0.93.0 data-plane YAML is not registered in contracts/manifest.json sources. The string only appears elsewhere as a schema-id namespace prefix inside contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/operations.json. By contrast the management row's activeSourceId is validated against the manifest at red_team_management.py:310-311, and the five frozen rows reuse verified frozen source ids. The result is one of seven source-precedence records whose active identity is an unverified label, in a file whose stated purpose is "seven explicit frozen/active source pairs ... and verifier/overlay ownership" (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:35-37).
findings.required_fix: Either add an "id" to contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/source.json and resolve the data-plane activeSourceId from that file (asserting it matches), or register the vendored data-plane source in contracts/manifest.json and resolve it the same way as the management source, so no row carries an identifier that no registry can confirm.

findings.description: Six intermediate private-material receipts are committed for this phase - phase-21-private-material-initial.json, -interrupted.json, -pre-oracle.json, -pre-scope-correction.json, -attempt-01.json and -attempt-02.json - alongside the one receipt the gate actually verifies, docs/checks/phase-21-private-material.json. Grepping docs/phase-status.json for phase-21-private-material returns no hits, so none of the six is referenced from the authoritative status file, unlike phase 20 which records its scans under candidate_private_scan and final_private_scan. A reader cannot tell which receipts are superseded working artifacts and which carry standing obligations, and the names alone imply unfinished state ("interrupted", "pre-scope-correction").
findings.required_fix: Record the phase-21 scan history in docs/phase-status.json under the phase 21 entry, naming the authoritative receipt and marking the intermediate ones as superseded with the reason each was regenerated, or remove the superseded receipts and keep only the gate-verified one plus a single provenance note.

findings.description: Routing CI to phase 21 removes the last committed-content whitespace check from remote execution. commands_for(21) contains only the unranged git diff --check and its --cached variant (tools/check_phase.py:139-140), both of which inspect nothing on the clean checkout CI produces, and the ranged b65f3c9..HEAD check that ran under the phase-20 subset is no longer selected. docs/CI.md:141-148 describes the phase 17/12/20 ranged exclusions and then asserts "Every owned source file retains the whitespace check", which now holds only for a developer's uncommitted work. No remote run of the re-pointed workflow exists either, so phase-21 CI coverage is configuration plus local guards only; docs/CI.md:161-162 and docs/PHASES.md:176-178 state that limitation honestly, which is why this is low rather than higher.
findings.required_fix: Either add a ranged hygiene command to management_commands(21) covering the management baseline (for example git diff --check against MANAGEMENT_BASELINE..HEAD with the three vendor exclusions) and extend tools/test_management_phases.py:120-124 to require it, or state plainly at docs/CI.md:141-148 that the current gate validates only uncommitted and staged whitespace and that committed-range hygiene returns with the phase-22 routing.

evidence: Recorded check evidence is complete, source-bound and real: docs/reviews/phase-21-attempt-01.checks.json:2-6 records phase 21, source_sha256 e2a407ab7c6f413a9b6651011e00c4b9f765dee0761f0e29b2710eee9d308694 (the reviewed hash), source_unchanged true, checked_at 2026-10-19T13:00:35.930783+00:00, passed true, and no "scope" key, so review_phase.check_evidence:203 would not reject it as a contracts-only receipt. Its 23 entries match tools/check_phase.py:135-170 management_commands(21) element for element and in order: the frozen baseline diff with the planning-fixture exclusion (:9-27), the verify_planning_fixture/gateway guard (:54-57), the untracked-SDK-file assertion (:71-80), the ten common commands including the vendor-excluded hygiene diffs (:88-134) and red_team_management --check --verify-retention-origin (:186-204), then test_ci.py, three generator --check tools, verify_native_fixtures --require-test-bindings, red_team_dataplane --check --require-complete, schema-oracle, verify-gateway-specimens, generate_validation and generate_models. Every entry has a resolved invocation array, exit_code 0 and timeout false; docs/checks/phase-21.json carries the identical phase, hash, timestamp and passed flag with no scope key.

Executed suites are green and substantive, with captured stderr in the snapshot: test_red_team_management.py "Ran 23 tests ... OK" (:231), test_management_phases.py "Ran 18 tests ... OK" (:260) and test_review_phase.py "Ran 51 tests ... OK" (:289). check_phase.require_nonempty_tests (check_phase.py:24-32) prevents an empty discovery pattern from passing silently. tools/verify-contracts.py --self-test stdout lists 27 rejected tampering cases (:182) including the ten new vendor-ownership cases: unowned-vendor-file, missing-vendor-file, modified-vendor-file, vendor-license-commit, duplicate-source-id, vendor-artifact-origin, vendor-artifact-omission, vendor-artifact-escape, vendor-symlink and unowned-vendor-version.

Provenance chain verified by reading end to end: tools/red_team_management.py:27 pins docs/research/2026-10-19-prisma-airs-openapi/inventory.json by sha256; that file at :44-54 records upstream sha256 5fbb533b... for the management spec at commit 582e30543bf2 with activeBytesEqualUpstream false; red_team_management.py:319-320 checks the vendored contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/mp-openapi.yaml against that hash; :341-345 requires the normalized openapi.json to parse equal to the YAML; contracts/manifest.json:1950-1963 and contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/source.json:13-15 record the same sha256, gitBlobSha1 9959caca... and 212515 bytes, with usedForGeneration false and license pan-dev-582e30543bf2 (MIT, licenseSha256 283becab..., identical to the data-plane LICENSE).

Vendor ownership is correctly scoped: tools/verify-contracts.py:29 limits VENDOR_ROOTS to contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0; :471-478 sweeps the parent directory and rejects any file outside a registered version; :479-489 requires exact equality between the manifested corpus file set and the on-disk set, covering all five files in the new tree (the YAML source plus four vendorArtifacts at manifest.json:2442-2483). The data-plane 0.93.0 and Portkey trees are not in corpus_roots, so their dedicated verifiers retain ownership, exactly as docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:65-70 requires.

Inventory completeness and mapping are real: contracts/airs-operations.json contains 160 rows each carrying coverage "native_method_exists; static_mapping_only; not_live_acceptance", with full parameters, requestBody, responses, security, servers and reachableReferences (sample rows at :4-73); COUNTS at red_team_management.py:22 sums to 160 and matches contracts/airs-active-sources.json operationCounts 18/23/47/42/5/21/4; contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/operations.json carries exactly 42 operationIds; build() raises on any unmapped operation (:348-349) and on any mapping/row set mismatch (:362-363), and verify_native_binding (:222-227) rejects an unqualified binding and a missing inherent impl method.

Delta classification is complete and fails closed where it matters: contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/compatibility-decisions.json contains 68 kind rows and 68 category/decision pairs with no unclassified row; the nine removals are the eight three-element component removals (each carrying component_removed_or_renamed plus a successorReference that exists in the new schema set, COMPONENT_SUCCESSORS at red_team_management.py:53 covering exactly the four *ConnectionParamsBase names x -Input/-Output) plus the Body_upload format:binary row. I accounted for all 29 'changed' rows: 17 digest-pinned paths, 11 annotation-only 'documentation' rows and the one target-parameters row, so nothing currently reaches the fail-open path. disposition() raises on any delta path containing 'required', on a property literally named description/title/example, on security changes, on non-schema deltas and on parameter additions or removals other than the single profiling_status filter; tools/test_red_team_management.py:41-44, 67-83 and 119-126 execute those paths.

Retention floor is independent, immutable and complete: contracts/compatibility/airs-0.2.2-retention.json and contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json each contain 4279 baselineIds, which equals contracts/native-exports.json (3820) plus contracts/native-operations.json (448) plus 11 redTeamExtraMethods, so the seed covers the full current ledgers rather than a subset. retained_floor (red_team_management.py:265-291) loads the floor only from the hash-pinned seed, verifies auditedSourceCommit 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e and sdkVersion 0.2.2, rejects duplicate baselineIds and uses an additive-only subset; verify_retention_origin (:294-301) rehashes all six RETENTION_LEDGER_PATHS and ran under the phase-21-only flag. tools/test_red_team_management.py:163-198 proves removals, emptied rustPaths, a changed default and seed tampering are rejected while additions are allowed and never rewrite the floor.

The SDK is genuinely frozen with a byte-exact metadata exception: the recorded git diff --exit-code against 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e over crates/scm-sdk, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE and the six frozen ledgers exits 0, and the git ls-files --others assertion confirms no untracked SDK file. check_phase.require_only_hash_replacements:79-91 permits only 64-hex values occurring exactly once as quoted tokens and then requires full byte equality; verify_planning_fixture:93-120 applies it to crates/scm-sdk/src/fixtures/model-regressions.json and the oracle corpus, resolves the corpus path from the baseline object so "source" cannot be redirected, rejects symlinks and requires the rebound manifest hash to equal current contracts/manifest.json bytes; verify_planning_gateway_proof:123-132 allows exactly the two allowlisted input hashes and fails closed if the allowlist is incomplete. tools/test_management_phases.py:29-68, 83-91 and 93-118 prove reformatting, reindentation, value changes, input reordering and a third rebound hash all raise.

Plan claims checked against actual bytes and all held: contracts/vendor/red-team-management/0.86.0/compatibility-decisions.json:2297-2324 shows TargetConnectionType gaining only VERTEX_AI and N8N over the frozen eleven; openapi.json:5489-5500 ResponseMode gains REALTIME; :5300-5306 ProfilingStatusFilter is exactly NOT_STARTED/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED while :5288-5296 ProfilingStatus retains PARTIALLY_COMPLETE; :9054-9062 TargetStatusFilter narrows to DRAFT/ACTIVE from the seven frozen values at contracts/sources/pan-dev/.../mp-openapi.yaml:5881-5890, and the frozen ProfilingStatus at :3559-3569 does contain INIT and QUEUED, so every row of the plan's migration table is grounded; openapi.json:559-567 wires the new filter as anyOf ProfilingStatusFilter/null, matching the shape disposition() demands at red_team_management.py:176; :9431-9503 confirms the four Vertex fields, the three regex patterns and the writeOnly/format:password redaction of customer_sa_email; :4791-4803 and :4901-4922 confirm MultiTurnClientSessionConfig carries a vendor default of "client_session" appended after stateful/stateless, which is precisely the default the plan refuses to insert so that {} still resolves stateless; frozen mp-openapi.yaml:1713-1732 confirms BasicAuthAuthConfig had no additionalProperties:false, so basic_username/basic_password really were tolerated unknown keys.
